## Maintain a live ledger
After each demo arrives, before choosing the next action:

Before each additional `request_demos`, identify at least two live hypotheses and one concrete property of a future example that would make their predictions diverge. description: Use when nested square/rectangular color bands appear to reverse their layer order.

# Continual-ARC concentric ring reversal

Use when an input contains one or more nested, axis-aligned rectangular/square frames made of uniform-color layers, potentially with a solid center. A demo can indicate that the output preserves each object’s dimensions and geometry but reverses the ordered colors of the concentric layers.

## Evidence and rule
- Represent each object as a sequence of colors from outside to inside: `[c0, c1, ..., ck]`.
- If demos support reversal, recolor the outermost layer with `ck`, the next layer with `c(k-1)`, and so on; the innermost region receives `c0`.
- Apply independently to each nested object, including a uniform filled center as the innermost layer. Preserve background, object boundaries, dimensions, and all coordinates.
- Do not infer a global color substitution: the same color may map differently depending on its layer role/object. This is a positional reversal of each object’s layer sequence.

## Verification
1. Confirm demo input/output boundaries and layer counts match.
2. List each object’s input layer colors outside-in and compare against output outside-in; require exact reversal for every demo object before using the rule.
3. Reconstruct the test output by changing color values only within the matching layers. Keep all background cells unchanged.
4. Check grid dimensions and every row length before submission.

## Demonstrated instance
A demo showed nested objects whose outside-in layer sequences reversed exactly in the output. The held-out test also used differently sized nested objects and solid centers; each object independently followed this reversal. Treat that as evidence for the general operation, not a task-specific color mapping.",
